stories.title: Malaysia urges ASEAN action as haze pushes air readings to unhealthy levels
stories.summary: Malaysia urges ASEAN to strengthen preventive measures against transboundary haze as air quality worsens to unhealthy levels in several areas. The country stresses collective action under the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution and welcomes ASEAN Secretariat's coordinating role. Prolonged dry weather and El Nino may worsen haze; Malaysia calls for increased surveillance, enforcement of burning restrictions, and firefighting readiness regionally. Malaysia has urged ASEAN member states to step up preventive measures and preparedness against transboundary haze as dry weather conditions push air quality to unhealthy levels in parts of the country. Malaysia’s Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Arthur Joseph Kurup said the country remained committed to the regional goal of achieving a haze-free ASEAN by 2030 through the effective implementation of the ASEAN Agreement on Transboundary Haze Pollution (AATHP). He said Malaysia had conveyed its position through an official message to ASEAN secretary-general Kao Kim Hourn on Aug 21. The call came as 11 areas in Sarawak and Melaka recorded unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am on Aug 22, according to the Air Pollutant Index Management System. Serian recorded the highest API reading in Malaysia at 190, followed by Kuching (181), Samarahan (177), Sri Aman (174), Sarikei (172), Sibu (160), Bintulu (157), Samalaju (156), Mukah (156), Miri (152) and Bukit Rambai in Melaka (140). Kurup said prolonged dry weather in the southern ASEAN region had resulted in an increase in hotspots and haze activity. He said the situation could worsen as the El Nino phenomenon was expected to strengthen gradually over the coming months. “Although fires are currently still under control within the respective borders of ASEAN member states, the risk of transboundary haze requires collective preparedness and heightened vigilance at the regional level,” he said in a statement on Aug 22. Kurup said transboundary haze pollution caused by land and forest fires must be addressed collectively through preventive action, national preparedness and continuous monitoring based on the principles of the AATHP.
